newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium should sell rest of Sabena, Belgacom -OECD.
newsitem.headline: Belgium should sell rest of Sabena, Belgacom -OECD.

text.p: The Belgian state should sell off its remaining interests in state airline Sabena and telephone operator Belgacom, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said on Tuesday.
"For air transport, Belgium has not yet decided on full privatisation of Sabena, the national carrier. This would appear advisable, though," the OECD said in a report on the country's economy.
"Likewise, in telecommunications, full privatisation of Belgacom is not yet being seriously considered, but probably should be," it added.
Belgium has already sold 49 percent of Sabena to Swissair and 49 percent of Belgacom to a consortium of other telephone companies including Ameritech, Tele Danmark and Singapore Telecom.
Sabena prices and costs were at the higher end of the industry in the OECD area and the company had had financial difficulties for years, the OECD said.
"Air transport has turned into a dynamic consumer market and the Belgian government presumably has little comparative expertise in the strategic management of air transport firms," it added.

The government said Belgian government attempts at regulating the telecoms sector and delivering a public service might also be better replaced by a system of tendering for the private supply of certain public services.
